title: Extension of a pulled coherent formal system to a fixed proper compactification
statement: Let $S,Z,Y,X$ be schemes, with $Z,Y,X$ Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $f:Z\to S$ be separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $J$ a quasi-coherent ideal on $S$, and $Q=J\mathcal O_Z$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal]. Let $G$ be a coherent formal $Q$-module [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] whose level $1$ support is proper over $S$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. Let $q:Y\to Z$ and $p:X\to S$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and $j:Y\to X$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], with $pj=fq$. There exists a coherent formal $J\mathcal O_X$-module $H$ whose termwise tensor pullback along $j$ is isomorphic to the termwise tensor pullback of $G$ along $q$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. This is extension of a formal system only; neither completion of a coherent module nor adic completeness is asserted.

source.place: Theorem Tag 088E, theorem-grothendieck-existence, proof: paragraph after Chow’s lemma, through formation of the extended coherent formal system; Lemma Tag 0CYJ, lemma-pushforward-coherent-on-open

proof.text: Use formal-systems pullback to form the coherent formal system on Y for Q.comap q. Use constant support and finite-type pullback support to identify the support of every level with the inverse image of the support of G at op 0. Proper inverse images of closed subsets proper over S are proper over S.

Map this support under j. Since p is proper and hence separated, closed-subset proper-over-base properties make its image T closed in X. It lies inside j(Y). Identify Y with the open range U of j, and use coherent pushforward on an open with closed ambient support to extend every level by zero, coherently on X.

Direct image sends the transition maps to compatible transition maps. The covering U and X minus T detects all required identities. On U, pullback is restriction and the ideal is Q.comap q by comap_comp, hQ and hj. Restriction preserves colimits, and the ideal-power-product image identity identifies the restricted power product; consequently the quotient-transition isomorphisms are the given ones. On X minus T, every extended level, its power product, and its quotient are zero. The power-product annihilation identity therefore holds globally. The transition factors through the quotient globally since it kills the power-product image; its factor is an isomorphism on both opens and hence globally. This gives IsCoherentFormalModule (J.comap p) for the extended system.

The restriction/direct-image counit for the open immersion is an isomorphism at every level and is natural in each transition map. Identify tensor pullback with restriction using the open-immersion part of exists_formalSystemsPullback. Assemble its component isomorphisms as a natural isomorphism of the two inverse systems. Package the extended system with the verified adic conditions to obtain H.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_chow_formal_system_extension
    {S Z Y X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian Z] [IsNoetherian Y] [IsNoetherian X]
    (f : Z ⟶ S) [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (J : S.IdealSheafData) (Q : Z.IdealSheafData) (hQ : Q = J.comap f)
    (G : CoherentFormalModule Z Q)
    (hR : Scheme.Modules.HasSupportProperOver f (G.obj.obj (op 0)))
    (q : Y ⟶ Z) [IsProper q] (p : X ⟶ S) [IsProper p]
    (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] (hj : j ≫ p = q ≫ f) :
    ∃ H : CoherentFormalModule X (J.comap p),
      Nonempty (G.obj ⋙ Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback q ≅
        H.obj ⋙ Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback j)
